newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada T-bills open little changed in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Canada T-bills open little changed in quiet trade.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened little changed in very quiet trade on Tuesday with the market largely awaiting direction from upcoming economic news and data, dealers said.

"I'm sensing a tremendous apathy towards the front end of the market. I think we're just kind of looking for some new direction," said one T-bill dealer with a bank-owned brokerage. "It's very stable right now. I haven't seen anything from clients."
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 2.85 percent from 2.86 percent at Monday's close.

Activity was light with the Quebec traders away for the St Jean Baptiste Day public and market holiday in Quebec. The weekly auction of government of Canada T-bills -- usually held on a Tuesday -- this week has been moved to Wednesday.

"It's very quiet and the market seems to have discounted the Japanese prime minister's remarks yesterday," said another dealer with a bank-owned brokerage. "We think maybe there's a little bit of room to back up here because of supply."
Both Canadian and U.S. markets weakened yesterday after Ryutaro Hashimoto said stable exchange rates are critical to Japan maintaining its holdings of U.S. bonds.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.14 percent from 3.15 percent. The one-year T-bill firmed to yield 3.61 percent from 3.63 percent.
The call loan or overnight lending rate traded at 3.0 percent, in the middle of the Bank of Canada's 2.75-3.25 percent target range.
